purpose: Check existing SPR fit-centre projection as a geometric alternative to multi-image neighbour machinery; no production adoption
selection: Exactly the six retained physically-near bottom-corner single-mirror raw-det failures; exclude four top-side points
input: Existing initial geometry ledger: 5000 actual soil coordinates, 2060 fixed IDs, J=1; no images or artificial source particles
reuse: Pure support/cubic from upl_wall_geometry_r1.py via upl_wall_topshift_r1.py; shifted constant/affine reconstruction uses the latter pure fit unchanged
projection: JSphCpuSingle.cpp:275-290: only if original target violates a real half-space by >1e-6*dp, project sequentially to one-dp clearance, real plane order left/bottom/right, max128 iterations and stop residual<=1e-6*dp
evaluation: Actual own-face reflection at x=0/x=4/z=0 stays the evaluation mirror. Only the fit centre moves; return fitted-intercept and nearest-sample-anchor values to that original mirror using q=-physical gradient.
physical_eligibility: Original fixed coordinate must remain within2h=.096m of real initial soil, unchanged
det_gate: Original abs(raw unscaled a_corr2 determinant)>=1e-3; no rescaling or relaxation
singular_policy: Report original rank/determinant/condition without any original inverse. Only shifted rank3 matrices passing the original determinant gate receive constant/affine reproduction calculations.
reproduction: Record original-mirror value and physical-gradient errors without a new numerical or physical acceptance threshold
arithmetic: Binary64 offline Cubic W/Fac and numpy matrix operations, exact XML wall planes. Not actual initialized float-normal plane offsets, CPU/GPU float kernel arithmetic, sorted accumulation or 0-ULP proof.
limitations: Initial geometry only. Not stress/NoSlip parity, force/flux acceptance, nonlinear field accuracy or deformed support validity; different fitting support can change non-affine results.
protected: No production/input/old record edits; no solver/build/Git/SHA; input metadata checked before/after
